persona.who: 29, chartered accountant in Indore, married 1 year, lives with in-laws who expect her to give up the practice after a baby. Husband avoids the topic.
persona.note: my mother in law keeps saying once the baby comes you will anyway leave all this CA work. I built my practice from zero. my husband just changes the subject. I feel like I am slowly being erased

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call being seen as less than you are, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from being erased in your own home to standing in the life you built, with the words to say so.

week_beats.hook: You recognise being erased, and the anger of it, named without blame.

understanding.core_struggle: A woman who built a CA practice from nothing is being told by her mother-in-law she will leave it after the baby, while her husband changes the subject.
understanding.mirror: Your practice is the thing they cannot see, and your husband is the one who looks away when they say it.
understanding.insight: You are not asking for too much. You are being handed a smaller picture of yourself than the one you live, and the smallness is theirs.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

queries.hook: Tension with my in-laws. Being seen as less than you are by the people who ought to know you best, and the anger of watching the life you built get called a phase.
queries.diagnose: When others see only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.
queries.story: A woman of learning and standing, dismissed by her husband's family, who questioned them openly and stood in her truth until they had no answer.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verse.line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.

matched.label: I want to change careers but I'm scared

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on a battlefield, explaining that true perfection lies in doing the work that comes naturally to you, even if it is flawed, rather than perfectly performing a role that is not yours. He tells Arjuna that whatever one is born to do, however imperfectly, is better than another's duty done perfectly. The work born of your own nature carries no fault, because the focus is on the offering, not on flawless results.
verse.for_you: You built this practice from nothing. That is your own work. The mother-in-law's words try to place you in a role that is not yours. You do not need to perform it perfectly or let it define you. Your own path, however imperfectly walked, is the only one that fits you.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verse.sanskrit: मुक्ताभिमानी मुक्तो हि बद्धो बद्धाभिमान्यपि । किंवदन्तीह सत्येयं या मतिः सा गतिर्भवेत् ॥
verse.line: Believe you are free and you are. Believe you are bound and you are. As you think, so you become.
verse.translation: One who thinks 'I am free' is free, and one who thinks 'I am bound' stays bound. The saying here is true: as you think, so you become.
verse.why: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.
verse.misuse: This is about inner freedom; it does not deny real constraints or problems that need action.

prasang.title: Janaka asks the boy-sage how to be free
prasang.summary: King Janaka, ruler of Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra three questions: how to gain wisdom, freedom and dispassion. Ashtavakra answers at once: you are not the body or your roles but the awareness that watches them, and freedom is available now.
prasang.story_hook: A powerful king bowed before a boy whose body was bent in eight places, and asked him how to be free.
prasang.lesson: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

verse.meaning: King Janaka, who rules Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person finds freedom. Ashtavakra answers that you are not your body or your roles, but the awareness that watches them. He says you are more than your roles and worries. Freedom is available right now. The verse tells us that what you believe about yourself becomes your reality. If you believe you are bound by your family or your work, you will feel bound. If you believe you are free, you begin to live as free.
verse.for_you: Your in-laws are trying to shrink your picture of yourself, but the reality is already there. When you think of your practice and your worth, you are not just imagining it. You are seeing what is already true.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verse.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
verse.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.for_you: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verse.sanskrit: त्वय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ विश्ववीचिः स्वभावतः । उदेतु वास्तमायातु न ते वृद्धिर्न वा क्षतिः ॥
verse.line: Let the waves of the world rise or fall. You, the ocean, neither gain nor lose.
verse.translation: In you, the boundless ocean, let the waves of the world rise or fall by their own nature. You neither grow nor shrink.
verse.why: You are the ocean, not the waves; let them rise and fall without losing yourself.

prasang.title: You are not your mind
prasang.summary: Ashtavakra drives home that Janaka is not the body, the doer, or the mind's likes and dislikes, but the ocean in which the waves of life rise and fall. He urges faith, an end to grief, and rest from endless deliberation.
prasang.lesson: You are the ocean, not the waves; let them rise and fall without losing yourself.

verse.meaning: Ashtavakra tells Janaka that he is the boundless ocean, not the waves. Let the world rise and fall around him. He neither grows nor shrinks. He is the stillness beneath the noise, and the waves cannot change his depth.
verse.for_you: The self cannot be cut, burned or made less; what they see is a role, and you were never only a role.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verse.sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Speak words that don't wound, that are true, kind and helpful. That is discipline of speech.
verse.translation: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
verse.why: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.
verse.misuse: Kind speech doesn't mean avoiding hard truths; it means saying them without cruelty.

prasang.title: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna, laying out what real effort looks like. He says that true austerity of speech is not silence or empty words. It is speaking in a way that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial. This is not about being soft or hiding the truth. It is about saying what is real without cruelty, offering words that do not wound the one who hears them. It is the discipline of using your voice to build up rather than tear down.
verse.for_you: When you tell your partner the truth about your practice and your worth, speak it without cruelty. Let your words be true, kind and helpful. Let them land as a steady fact, not an attack.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu is teaching Nidagha how a free person lives among others without losing themselves. Ribhu says to always do the work that comes, to see friend and foe with the same eye, and to be free of wanting and not wanting. Such a person neither grieves nor craves. Ribhu adds that this person speaks what is agreeable to all, speaks gently when asked, and knows the intent of others' hearts, so they do not sink in the world. Ribhu is showing that you can live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.
verse.for_you: You built a CA practice from zero, and now you are being told it will end with a baby. Do the work in front of you. Speak gently when asked, but know the intent in your mother-in-law's heart, and do not sink in their story. You are the ocean, and their words are only waves.

story.title: Gargi questions Yajnavalkya at Janaka's court
story.story_hook: In a hall full of the most learned men in the land, one woman stood up twice.
story.summary: King Janaka offers a thousand cows to the wisest scholar. Yajnavalkya claims them and is challenged by one learned man after another. Gargi, the only woman, rises twice like a warrior with two arrows, then graciously tells the hall none of them can beat him. Yajnavalkya closes by asking what root a person grows from when cut down by death.
story.lesson: Ask your hard questions bravely, and give credit where it is due.

anchor.speaker: Yajnavalkya
anchor.setting: At King Janaka's debate, Kahola asks about the self.
anchor.sanskrit: या ह्येव पुत्रैषणा सा वित्तैषणा या वित्तैषणा सा लोकैषणोभे ह्येते एषणे एव भवतस्तस्माद्ब्राह्मणः पाण्डित्यं निर्विद्य बाल्येन तिष्ठासेत् । बाल्यं च पाण्डित्यं च निर्विद्याथ मुनिरमौनं च मौनं च निर्विद्याथ ब्राह्मणः ।
anchor.line: Wanting children, wanting money, wanting status: it is one desire. Learn, then live with a child's simplicity.
anchor.translation: The desire for sons is the desire for wealth, and the desire for wealth is the desire for worlds; both are just desires. So a wise man, having done with learning, should seek to live like a child. Having done with both childlike simplicity and learning, he becomes a sage; having done with both silence and its absence, he becomes a true knower.
anchor.why: Ask your hard questions bravely, and give credit where it is due.

story.for_you: You have asked the hard questions and you have named the truth. Now you can see the roots of their smallness. Live with the simplicity of someone who knows what they are worth.

script: You feel angry and erased right now. Someone in your home is trying to shrink the life you built. You are not asking for too much. You are being handed a smaller picture of yourself than the one you live, and the smallness is theirs.
On a battlefield, Arjuna is paralyzed by grief and duty. Krishna stands beside him and points out that the work born of your own nature carries no fault. And Krishna replied:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्, स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्.
In plain words: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.

This is easier said than done, because the people around you will keep measuring you against their script. They want you to perform a role that is not yours. The truth underneath is that your own path, walked with all its flaws, is the only one that carries no wrong. The focus is on the offering of your work, not on flawless results.

Your practice was built from nothing by you. The mother-in-law's words try to place you in a role that is not yours. You do not need to perform it perfectly or let it define you. Your own path is the only one that fits.
Your own work carries no fault.

depth.life: Your partner changes the subject when your mother-in-law says you will leave your CA practice after the baby. You built this practice from nothing, and now you are being erased in your own home.
depth.points: The texts say you incur no wrong by doing the work born of your own nature. The mother-in-law's words are not your truth. They are an attempt to place you in a role that is not yours.
depth.practice: When your partner changes the subject, hold the thought that your practice is yours alone. Let it sit in your chest for a moment without speaking.
depth.question: What part of your work feels most like your own nature right now?
